column1: # Star Fox (Switch 2, update v131072). In bring-up on the Mac: see README.md
# Its engine "eclipse" (Bullet, Granny, Wwise 2024.1, NPLN, libuv), SDK 21.4.4 built for the Switch 2 (Ounce), NVN2 (Ampere shaders); modules main + subsdk0 (movie) + subsdk3 (nn::camera) + sdk.
# Packed from a NUP (base + update 131072). Shaders: bare records in data.zip (VZIP, linked LZ4 chunks) and VIPR packs (shader_split.py).
# the NUP's update carries no display version: v131072 is a placeholder
# not loaded, main takes nothing from them the host does not supply: subsdk1 (C / libc), subsdk2 (NintendoSDK_DLSS: the host implements NVN2's DLSS on MetalFX)
# the RomFS holds two files: data.zip (14.5 GB) and a .cvar file
# data.zip's members are LZ4 already: stored, not compressed again
# The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB (Donkey Kong Bananza's figure). The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so virtual address memory is on, and main sets no heap.
# Set by hand for the first build: the SDK 21 Switch 2 split of Splatoon Raiders, which ships the same sdk build (41d4de4a…) and needs its 16 GB alias region (docs/reference/memory.md).
# The survey's guess, a 5 GB block with a 4.375 GB alias region, is less than the game maps: up to +8.53 GB in a session's log
# No fps_target: the game sets its own present interval (1, and 2 in some stretches; frame time p50 16.67 ms in headless runs), and main has neither a frame step
# nor an engine frame limit the host writes, so the host would not apply a target (hle_nvn.c fps_present_cap) and the Frame rate setting would do nothing
# shader inputs: kept as the provisional profile had them
# the game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode with near = 0 (found by the NSP script's address region check, which found no address regions)
